hero.name: Waren Spacefarer
hero.heroLook: Lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, wearing a worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots.

quests.title: Buy the Kestrel

quests.title: Deliver the Grubstake to Vesta
quests.detail: Fly the tug to Vesta for six hundred credits.

quests.title: Stop Vasko's burn
quests.detail: Kill the Grubstake's drive before Vasko flees.

summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot with ten credits, wants forty thousand credits to buy the Kestrel from Marta Okafor. He took a relief pilot job on the ore tug Grubstake for Captain Dren Vasko, who smuggles people in the sealed hold. When Ceres Customs boarded, Vasko fused the airlock, fought Waren, then ran to the cockpit to burn. Waren warned customs, who pulled their collar free, then he pulled the main drive breaker below decks and killed the burn. Customs is clamping back on. Vasko is coming down the ladder toward Waren, who holds the bolt gun and has badly hurt ribs. The Vesta job is probably lost.

facts: Marta Okafor will sell the Kestrel to Waren for forty thousand credits.
Vasko promised Waren six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta.
Ceres Customs is boarding the Grubstake.
People are trapped in the Grubstake's sealed hold, begging for help.
Customs detached from the Grubstake after Waren's warning and asked him to stop the drive.
Waren killed the Grubstake's main drive breaker; the tug can't burn.

recent.action: Unlock the airlock for the customs team
recent.narration:
You lunge for the airlock panel. Your fingers are on the release when the locker slams open behind you.

Vasko is faster. He drives you into the hatch frame shoulder-first, and something cold and blunt presses under your ribs: a cargo bolt gun, the kind used to pin crates. Your sore jaw throbs against the metal.

"Hands off the panel," he breathes. Outside, the docking collar clanks home. A gloved fist pounds the outer hatch. "Customs! Open up!"

Behind you, from the sealed hold, the knocking turns into a voice. Muffled, desperate, human: "Help us! Please!"

Vasko's eyes flick toward the sound. For one second, the bolt gun drifts.
recent.picture: Cramped airlock corridor of an old ore tug, red emergency lights. A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over grey t-shirt, cargo pants, scuffed boots, pinned against a hatch frame, hand reaching for a release panel; a wiry man in his forties, gaunt face, shaved head, hard pale eyes, stained brown work jacket, heavy boots, pressing an industrial tool against him.

recent.narration:
You slap at the release, but your palm skids off the panel. Vasko's distracted second ends in a flat, ugly thunk: the bolt gun fires into the panel beside your hand. Sparks spray. Fragments of hot plastic sting your knuckles, and his elbow catches your ribs on the way down.

The panel dies with a whine. The airlock is fused shut.

Outside, the pounding stops. A new sound starts: the low hiss of a cutting torch biting into the outer hatch. A glowing orange line creeps across the metal.

Vasko reloads, breathing hard. "Ten minutes before they're through," he mutters. "Get up and fly, or get out of my way."

From the hold, the voices have gone quiet, listening.

He's thumbing a fresh bolt into the chamber when you hit him low, the way your uncle taught you in the dock gym. You both slam into the deck. The bolt gun clatters away and skids under a cargo strap rack.

Vasko is wiry and mean. His knee finds your bruised ribs and the pain goes white, but you get your forearm across his throat and your weight on his chest. He thrashes, then goes still and glares up at you.

"You think they'll thank you?" he rasps. "They'll lock up the people in that hold too. Send them back to wherever they ran from."

The orange line on the hatch is a third of the way around. The hold is silent.
recent.picture: Cramped airlock corridor of an old ore tug, red emergency lights, a glowing orange cutting line on a hatch. A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots, pinning to the deck a wiry man in his forties, gaunt face, shaved head, hard pale eyes, stained brown work jacket, heavy boots.

recent.action: Grab the bolt gun and hold him
recent.narration:
You shift your weight to reach under the rack. That's all Vasko needs. He bucks, twists, and drives his heel into your bruised ribs. You fold, gasping, fingers brushing cold metal and losing it.

By the time you drag the bolt gun out, Vasko is gone, boots pounding up the ladder toward the cockpit. You hear the drive warm-up chime. He's going to burn with the customs cutter still clamped to the hatch.

The orange line is halfway around now. Somewhere behind the hold door, someone starts crying softly.

You stand there, ribs screaming, the bolt gun heavy in your hand. Cockpit, hold, or hatch.

recent.action: Shout a warning through the hatch
recent.narration:
You press your mouth to the hot seam and shout over the hiss. "He's starting the drive! Detach or you'll tear loose! There are people in the hold!"

The torch cuts out. A muffled voice answers, fast and clear: "Copy. Pulling the collar." Then, quieter: "Kid, can you kill that drive?"

Through the hull you hear the cutter's clamps release with a deep clunk. Up the ladder, the warm-up chime climbs toward its final tone. You have maybe a minute before Vasko burns.

The bolt gun is heavy in your hand. Your ribs still feel like they're full of glass.

recent.action: Pull the drive's main breaker below decks
recent.narration:
You drop down the engine ladder, half falling, ribs screaming. The drive bay is hot and loud, the reactor coupling humming up toward burn. The main breaker sits behind a mesh cage stencilled with warnings. You remember the old tug drills: cage latch, safety pin, then the handle all the way down.

The warm-up chime hits its last note just as you throw your whole weight on the lever.

It drops with a heavy clack. The hum dies. The lights flicker down to a dim red emergency glow.

Overhead, Vasko swears, long and loud. Then his boots start back down the ladder, fast.

Through the hull comes the clunk of the customs collar locking back on. In the hold, someone is knocking again, softly now, hopeful.
recent.picture: Cramped engine bay of an old ore tug in dim red emergency light. A lean young man in his early twenties, short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots, hanging his whole weight on a big breaker lever inside a mesh cage, sparks fading, pipes and machinery around him.
